usage: This is the standard way to ask if someone speaks English in Cairo. It is casual but perfectly acceptable for everyday interactions. When approaching a stranger, official, or someone older, Cairenes typically add the polite pronoun 7adretak to a man or 7adretek to a woman before the verb.

variants.label: to a man (casual)
variants.note: Default casual form for addressing a single male.

variants.label: to a woman (casual)
variants.note: Default casual form for addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when asking two or more people.

variants.label: to a man (formal)
variants.note: Polite form for male strangers, elders, or authority figures.

variants.label: to a woman (formal)
variants.note: Polite form for female strangers, elders, or authority figures.

examples.english: Excuse me, do you speak English?

examples.arabic: أنا مابتكلمش عربي كويس، حضرتك بتتكلم إنجليزي؟
examples.english: I don't speak Arabic well, do you speak English?

examples.arabic: يا جماعة، بتتكلموا إنجليزي ولا فرنساوي؟
examples.transliteration: ya gama3a, betetkallemu engleezi walla faransawi?
examples.english: Guys, do you speak English or French?
